messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: SEV-2: Suspicious auth traffic from service-account keys — large POSTs to logs-api from external IPs. PagerDuty P-4821 created. https://redwood.internal/incidents/P-4821 :rotating_light:
maya-oncall: I'm on it. Paging sec and SRE. Any immediate customer-facing alerts?
sam-sec: seeing a spike in auth failure and some successful calls using service-account-logger. Source IPs: 198.51.100.23, 203.0.113.77. Looks like tokens in env on an EC2 fleet.
lee-sre: confirmed concurrent long-running POSTs to /v1/logs with high data-out to 198.51.100.23. Throughput matches multiple GB/hr.
jordan-support: noticed a couple customers reported increased 401/403s ~ 5m ago. CS is triaging.
maya-oncall: quick mitigation plan: 1) disable the implicated service account keys 2) block external IPs at WAF + VPC SG 3) rotate any exposed API keys 4) notify customers if logs were exported. Agree?
sam-sec: agree. Prepare for key rotation. We should snapshot forensic data first. @lee-sre can you take a pcap and backup logs?
lee-sre: running collector now, saving to s3://redwood-incident-evidence/P-4821/ — will notate chain of custody. Command:
```
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host 198.51.100.23 -w /tmp/p4821.pcap
aws s3 cp /tmp/p4821.pcap s3://redwood-incident-evidence/P-4821/ --acl private
```
lee-sre: WAF rule applied to block both IPs, propagation in ~30s. Also adding temporary rate-limit on /v1/logs route.
ops-bot: WAF update applied: rule id wf-9832 blocked 198.51.100.23,203.0.113.77. Rate-limit 60r/m on /v1/logs.
maya-oncall: sam, can you disable the specific IAM access key? It's `AKIA********EXAMPLE` (placeholder in logs) — don't rotate whole account yet, just disable key.
sam-sec: disabling now via console and issuing rotation orders to infra. Command used: `aws iam update-access-key --access-key-id AKIAEXAMPLE --status Inactive --user-name service-account-logger` — confirmed inactive.
maya-oncall: Confirmed inbound traffic for that key dropped to zero. Good. Next: rotate all keys for service-account-logger, and search for any other service accounts exhibiting similar behavior.
sam-sec: starting bulk search: query logs for access_key_id pattern `AKIA` with high egress.
lee-sre: found 3 EC2 instances launched by the infra onboarding job in us-east-1 with environment variable LOG_KEY set. Instances: i-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h, i-0h7g6f5e4d3c2b1a. Suspect compromised AMI.
jordan-support: Customer impact update: two enterprise customers reported spikes in data export and transient 403s; support ticket numbers #CS-9871, #CS-9872. They're asking if logs were exfiltrated.
amal-legal: (typo, corrected) ana-legal: copying legal. Need exact scope before customer disclosure. Preserve evidence.
maya-oncall: Sam, Lee — collect list of objects transferred out of /v1/logs for the affected timeframe (T0-30m to T0+10m). Also check for S3 PUTs to external endpoints.
sam-sec: query running, outputting list to evidence bucket. Preliminary: 4 large POSTs completed, ~1.2GB total to external IPs. Unknown where stored on remote side.
lee-sre: we rotated the AMI and removed the compromised instances from autoscaling groups. Terminating instances now.
ops-bot: EC2 termination commands executed for i-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h and i-0h7g6f5e4d3c2b1a. Autoscale group detached.
maya-oncall: Handoff: I'm going to start incident bridge and then hand off to sam-sec for containment. @sam-sec you become incident lead in 15m unless you pass it back. Bridge: meet via Zoom https://zoom.redwood/incident-P-4821 (start now).
sam-sec: taking lead. Will coordinate with infra to issue key rotations and KMS double-check. Plan to rotate service-account-logger keys, invalidate sessions, and run a Diff to see which log batches were affected.
jordan-support: CS: notifying affected customers with tentative timeframe and we are investigating potential log exposure. Message queued for approval by legal.
nana-legal: ana-legal: request to preserve any chat/email with vendor s3 endpoints and vendor contract for disclosure. Also need to create CISO ticket.
sam-sec: started scripted rotation:
```
# rotate keys for service-account-logger
aws iam create-access-key --user-name service-account-logger > /tmp/new_key.json
# update deployments to use new key
kubectl set env deployment/logshipper LOGGER_KEY=$(jq -r .AccessKey.AccessKeyId /tmp/new_key.json)
```
sam-sec: note: we will also revoke AWS STS tokens tied to that key.
lee-sre: applied temporary read-only lock on logs-store bucket to prevent new PUTs from shipper while we verify integrity.
maya-oncall: Customer-facing messaging draft (for review):
"We detected unauthorized requests using a service account which may have accessed log data. We have contained the activity by disabling the compromised keys, blocking the source IPs, terminating the affected instances, and are rotating keys. We are investigating scope and will follow up within 24 hours."
amal-legal: ana-legal: tweak approved, add "no evidence at this time of exfiltration to vendor storage" only if confirmed. Otherwise say "may have accessed".
jordan-support: sending approved message to customers #CS-9871,#CS-9872 now.
sam-sec: Forensics update: pulled request/response bodies for suspicious POSTs. Two files show base64-encoded payloads consistent with logs. Hashes: sha256: abc123... (stored in evidence).
lee-sre: ACLs and KMS checks: keys used for encryption are intact; however, we found one IAM policy overly permissive allowing PutObject to arbitrary buckets. We'll tighten policy and roll out least-priv change.
maya-oncall: Okay immediate actions done. Next: 1) full key rotation for any service account with matching image 2) infra to audit AMI build process 3) legal/comms draft 4) postmortem owner = sam-sec + lee-sre.
sam-sec: creating internal incident ticket RWD-2026-4821 and linking playbook.
ops-bot: Incident RWD-2026-4821 created and linked to PD P-4821. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/compromised-keys
maya-oncall: handing off active monitoring to sam-sec. I'll remain on the bridge for the next 10m for questions then step down.
sam-sec: taking over. Current status: containment done, evidence collected, customer notifications sent to impacted subset, escalation to legal done. Ongoing: deeper data exfiltration analysis and AMI root cause.
anal-legal: ana-legal: requesting timeline for regulatory teams if confirmed exfiltration. Also please flag any GDPR/PII that might be present in logs.
jordan-support: CS will collate customer log examples to help with analysis.
lee-sre: estimated time to remediation (full rotation & AMI fix) ~ 6 hours. Will push hotfix to build pipeline to prevent embedding secrets in AMI.
maya-oncall: great. I'll close this thread when sam confirms all rotations completed and monitoring shows no further anomalous auth. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: UPDATE: P-4821 status changed to Investigating -> Mitigated at 1743564600. Logs archived: s3://redwood-incident-evidence/P-4821/manifest.json
maya-oncall: Mitigated — handing off to postmortem queue. Postmortem owner: @sam-sec. Add CS, legal, SRE reviewers.
sam-sec: will draft. Initial notes captured in shared doc: https://redwood.internal/docs/P-4821-postmortem
ops-bot: Reminder: schedule follow-up review in 48 hours."
